note: 100-point rubric for an X profile. Score each item 0 to its points, add the total, then rewrite the items that lost the most points first. Premium-only features (long bio links, badges) are deliberately not scored.

bands.0-64: rewrite the promise first, everything else depends on it

items.name: Bio states who it is for and what changes
items.passes_when: The bio says who you help and the concrete outcome, in plain words a stranger gets in 3 seconds.
items.fails_when: Job titles only, 'passionate about', a list of interests, or a promise with no object.
items.fix: Rewrite as: who you help + the result + one proof point.

items.name: Bio fits 160 characters and uses them
items.passes_when: Weighted length is 160 or less (run xcount.py) and not under 80.
items.fails_when: Cut off mid-thought, or a 40-character bio that wastes the space.
items.fix: Count it with xcount.py. Cut adjectives before nouns.

items.name: One real proof point
items.passes_when: A number, a named client type or a shipped thing the user supplied.
items.fails_when: Adjectives instead of evidence. Any figure the user did not give is a {{your number}} placeholder.
items.fix: Ask the user for one true number. Never invent it.

items.name: Pinned post is the best answer to 'why follow you'
items.passes_when: Pinned post is a single strong post (not a thread teaser) that shows the user's best thinking and ends with the path off-platform.
items.fails_when: Pinned post is old news, an announcement of a thread, or empty.
items.fix: Use /x-post to write one pinned post; link in the first reply, not the body.

items.name: A clear next step off X
items.passes_when: Header link or bio link goes to one place (newsletter, booking, product) and the bio says what is there.
items.fails_when: No link, a link tree of eight things, or a link that does not match the promise.
items.fix: One link, one promise, matching the bio.

items.name: Profile website field is used
items.passes_when: The website field points at the single destination.

items.name: Banner supports the promise
items.passes_when: Banner repeats or extends the promise in 6 words or fewer, readable on mobile, nothing important under the profile photo.
items.fails_when: Stock image, no text, or text hidden by the avatar.
items.fix: Short line, left-aligned away from the avatar, high contrast.

items.name: Name and handle are easy to say and match
items.passes_when: Display name is the real name or the brand; handle is short, no digits strings.
items.fails_when: Handle full of underscores and numbers, name stuffed with emoji or keywords.
items.fix: Keep the name plain. Put keywords in the bio.

items.name: Photo is a clear face or clear mark
items.fails_when: Tiny full-body shot, logo with illegible text.
items.fix: Crop to the face, plain background.

items.name: Profile reads in the same voice as the posts
items.passes_when: Bio, pinned post and last 5 posts sound like one person (check against voice.md).
items.fails_when: Corporate bio over casual posts, or the reverse.
items.fix: Rewrite the bio in the voice from voice.md.

items.name: No engagement bait or hype in the profile
items.passes_when: No 'follow for more', 'DM me for alpha', income claims, hashtag strings.
items.fails_when: Any of those. Income claims are also an Original Content Rewards risk.
